correctness.rationale: Exact definition and subset-monotonicity reduce maximality to all one-vertex extensions; every hypercube geodesic is a unique permutation of differing coordinate flips. XOR translation normalizes any nonempty set to contain zero. The exhaustive C++17 checker examines each of the 67,945,521 normalized seven-sets plus every smaller normalized cardinality, finding zero maximal below seven and exactly seven seven-sets, all closed neighborhoods. A separate Boolean interval dynamic-programming checker agrees on the 7,666,239 normalized sets of sizes two through six and verifies all 64 neighborhoods.

This result establishes both the six-cube lower number and *all* optimizer placements at a natural 64-vertex finite dimension, separating worst-case maximal greedy termination from the already-known optimum largest-set size. The rigidity statement is an exact natural combinatorial classification, useful as a benchmark for proposed all-dimensional bounds.
